people.label: Harold E. Puthoff
people.sub: President, EarthTech International Inc.; founder, Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin; former SRI International programme director; co-founder and VP Science & Technology, To The Stars Academy
people.narrative: Puthoff is the hinge on which the whole technical layer turns. He is a Stanford electrical-engineering PhD (1967, under Richard Pantell) who spent the 1970s and early 1980s running SRI International's classified psychoenergetics work with Russell Targ - the SRI half of what became the Stargate Project - which is the formative fact about him: he has been the government's outsourced handler for phenomena the government does not want on its own org chart for more than fifty years. In 1985 he founded the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, incorporated under EarthTech International in 1991, at 11855 Research Blvd, Austin - the address that appears on the cover of at least one Defense Intelligence Reference Document. Under the DIA Defense Warning Office's Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) programme in FY2009 he authored 'Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering', one of the 38 reference products the DIA listed to the Federation of American Scientists on 16 January 2019. He was not merely an author: the cover page of Christopher 'Kit' Green's DIRD on human injuries carries the imprint 'Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin' and its preface quotes a 'November 2007 Proposal to Analyze Probable ET Generated Specific Near-field Electromagnetic Emissions: to Puthoff/Hathaway' - meaning Puthoff was being solicited to organise medical reverse-engineering of putative extraterrestrial field effects nine months before the AAWSAP contract was awarded. In 2017 he co-founded To The Stars Academy with Tom DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Steve Justice, and his laboratories became the analytical destination for the ADAM Research Project's metamaterial samples. That is the custody problem in one man: the same physicist who tested Linda Moulton Howe's bismuth-magnesium laminate privately in the 1990s and 2000s, wrote a 2012 letter reporting no 'interesting/anomalous outcome', and then in 2019 sat inside the corporate entity that bought those same samples for $35,000 and put them under a five-year Army CRADA. He appeared as an interviewee in Dan Farah's 2025 documentary 'The Age of Disclosure'.

people.narrative: Davis is the single most important technical witness on this board because his key act is documented rather than merely asserted. He co-authored a second DIRD, 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions', with Richard Obousy. Davis is also the author of record of the notes of an alleged October 2002 meeting with Vice Adm. Thomas R. people.label: Garry P. Nolan
people.sub: Rachford and Carlota A. Harris Professor, Department of Pathology, Stanford University School of Medicine; co-founder, The Sol Foundation; member, UAP Science Advisory Council (2026)
people.narrative: Nolan is the most credentialed working scientist to put his name to UAP materials analysis, and the reason the subject now has a peer-reviewed footprint at all. He has held the Harris endowed chair in pathology at Stanford since 2011, founded Rigel, Nodality, BINA Technology (sold to Roche for $107m) and Akoya Biosciences, and co-developed CODEX and multiplexed ion beam imaging (MIBI) with Michael Angelo and Sean Bendall - the same MIBI instrument he then turned on alleged UAP debris. His entry into the field was not voluntary in the ordinary sense: he told KQED in June 2021 that he was approached by 'some people representing the government and an aerospace corporation to help them understand the medical harm that had come to some individuals, related to supposed interactions with an anomalous craft', because 'they were interested in the kinds of blood analysis that my lab can do'. That is the crux for this board - an unnamed government element and an unnamed aerospace corporation walking human casualty material into a Stanford pathology laboratory. In January 2022 he published, with Jacques Vallee, Sizun Jiang and former NASA Ames engineer Larry Lemke, the first serious peer-reviewed instrumental study of alleged UAP material in Progress in Aerospace Sciences, applying SIMS and MIBI at 200 nm lateral resolution to the 1977 Council Bluffs, Iowa molten-metal mass. The finding is genuinely awkward for both camps: no anomalous isotope ratios, but incomplete mixing of the constituent metals indicating an industrial process of unknown origin, with meteoritic, satellite, aircraft, dumping and thermite explanations each argued away. In May 2023 at the SALT iConnections conference he said governments have retrieved artefacts from extraterrestrial craft and put the probability of long-term extraterrestrial visitation at '100 percent'. He co-founded The Sol Foundation with Peter Skafish on 15 August 2023, and in June 2026 was named to the White House-requested UAP Science Advisory Council.

people.label: Jacques F. Vallee
people.sub: Computer scientist and venture capitalist; ARPANET-era researcher at SRI's Augmentation Research Center; NIDS consultant; keeper of the largest private anomalous-materials collection
people.narrative: Vallee is the provenance chain. Where Nolan brought the instruments, Vallee brought the samples and, crucially, the fifty-year paper trail attached to them. Trained in mathematics at Paris (1959) and astrophysics at Lille (1961), with a Northwestern PhD (1967), he joined Douglas Engelbart's Augmentation Research Center at SRI International in 1971 - the same institution and period as Puthoff's psychoenergetics work - and succeeded Paul Baran as principal investigator on the NSF computer-networking project, building PLANET, one of the first ARPANET conferencing systems. He then spent 1987-2010 as a Silicon Valley general partner. Across all of it he assembled a physical collection of alleged UAP-associated materials with documented case files: the 1957 Ubatuba magnesium fragments, the 1977 Council Bluffs molten mass, and the 1945 San Antonio, New Mexico 'Trinity' case material he wrote up with Paola Harris in 2021. He was a consultant to Robert Bigelow's National Institute for Discovery Science and a member of the Bigelow Aerospace scientific advisory board, which puts him inside the same Bigelow ecosystem that produced BAASS and the AAWSAP contract. His 2022 collaboration with Nolan is the moment the collection met modern instrumentation. The custody problem here is honest and stated: Vallee's samples come with newspaper reporting, police photographs, fire-department accounts and witness interviews - a civil chain, not a federal one - and that is exactly why the government-held material remains the missing term. His lifetime archive went to the Archives of the Impossible at Rice University, with embargoes running to 2028-2031: a dark segment with a published end date.

people.label: Christopher 'Kit' Green
people.sub: M.D., Ph.D., neuroscientist and forensic clinician; former CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence Life Sciences Division; author of the AAWSAP human-injury DIRD produced under the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin
people.narrative: Green is the medical end of the reverse-engineering programme, and his released DIRD is one of the most revealing documents in the entire corpus because of what it takes for granted. A physician-neuroscientist who ran life-sciences analysis for CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence before moving to General Motors and then Wayne State University, Green was the analyst to whom the intelligence community's biological anomalies were routed - including, in the 1970s, the SRI remote-viewing work. His AAWSAP paper, 'Clinical Medical Acute & Subacute Field Effects on Human Dermal & Neurological Tissues', was released publicly by Popular Mechanics on 14 February 2020, and its cover carries the imprint of Puthoff's Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin. Its preface quotes verbatim from a November 2007 proposal addressed 'to Puthoff/Hathaway' which states the intention plainly: 'certain characteristics of the fields associated with exotic propulsion can with near certainty be gleaned from archival records of their effects on human physiology.' Its Hypothesis One is that 'sufficient evidence exists from human injury / effects to reverse engineer certain aspects of the Energy / Propulsion Systems'. Its executive summary concludes that 'some advanced systems are already deployed, and opaque to full US Intelligence understanding'. It contains a Schuessler catalogue appendix, a 'Green-Morris Cases' appendix, and an ICD-diagnostics appendix built on 42 peer-reviewed cases plus roughly 300 unpublished ones, and it names the Cash-Landrum event. This is a US intelligence contractor document that treats humans injured by unidentified craft as an instrumented dataset for reverse engineering exotic propulsion.

people.narrative: Kelleher is the working scientist who ran the field side of the government's own anomalous-phenomena programme, and he is the reason the biological and materials strands are joined. A biochemist by training, he was a project manager at Robert Bigelow's National Institute for Discovery Science through its Skinwalker Ranch and animal-mutilation investigations, and in 2005 co-wrote 'Hunt for the Skinwalker' with George Knapp - the book that DIA official James Lacatski read, which prompted Lacatski to contact Bigelow, visit the ranch, and set in motion the sequence that produced Sen. Harry Reid's $22 million appropriation and the AAWSAP contract to BAASS. When that contract landed, Kelleher became deputy administrator of BAASS, which is to say the deputy director of the operational arm of a Defense Intelligence Agency programme. In 2021 he co-authored 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon' with Lacatski and Knapp, an account written by the programme's own manager and its own deputy administrator. That is a very unusual thing: the two people who ran the contract wrote the memoir. What they describe - biological effects on personnel, physical trace evidence, sample collection - is the same subject matter as Green's DIRD and Nolan's later laboratory work, and it is the connective tissue between the paranormal-adjacent field programme and the materials-analysis pipeline.

people.label: Abraham 'Avi' Loeb
people.sub: Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science, Harvard University; Director, Institute for Theory and Computation, Harvard-Smithsonian CfA; founder, The Galileo Project; Chair, UAP Science Advisory Council (2026)
people.narrative: Loeb is what happens when the technical layer refuses to wait for the classified system. Harvard astronomy faculty since 1993, tenured three years later, chair of the astronomy department 2011-2020, Baird Professor since 2012, and director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics since 2007, he founded The Galileo Project on 26 July 2021 - four weeks after the ODNI preliminary assessment - on the explicit premise that the way out of a classified impasse is to build unclassified instruments and publish. The project raised roughly $1.8 million in its first year from donors including Frank Laukien of Bruker and William Linton of Promega, installed its first observatory at Harvard College Observatory in 2022, and published its instrumentation architecture in the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation. In June-July 2023 he led a $1.6 million Pacific Ocean expedition off Papua New Guinea to recover fragments of CNEOS 2014-01-08 (IM1), returning with sub-millimetre spherules that his team classified as a distinct 'BeLaU' composition in Research Notes of the AAS and Chemical Geology. The scientific counter-attack was heavy and specific: Fernando et al. in Geophysical Journal International (March 2024) showed the guiding seismic signal was probably truck traffic; Gallardo argued coal-ash contamination in Research Notes of the AAS; Rudraswami et al. re-evaluated the spherules' origin in Chemical Geology in March 2025. Loeb conceded ground on 3I/ATLAS in 2025-2026 after speculating about its artificiality. Then on 15 June 2026 the position changed entirely: Loeb was named chair of a UAP Science Advisory Council formed at the request of the White House in coordination with AARO, ODNI, the FBI and other agencies - a council with, by contemporaneous reporting, no budget and no access to classified material.

people.label: Matthew Szydagis
people.sub: Associate Professor of Physics, University at Albany (SUNY); dark-matter instrumentation physicist (LUX/LZ, NEST); co-founder of UAPx; member, UAP Science Advisory Council (2026)
people.narrative: Szydagis is the instrumentation conscience of the field. His day job is liquid-xenon dark-matter detection - he is a principal author of the Noble Element Simulation Technique (NEST) and has published on xenon bubble chambers and low-energy nuclear recoils - which means his professional standard for what counts as a detection is set by an experiment that has spent decades not finding something. He also published in Limina, the journal of UAP studies, in March 2025 on disclosure timelines. In June 2026 he was named to the UAP Science Advisory Council in the instrumentation and data-collection role, which puts a working detector physicist on the government's outside science body.

people.label: Kevin H. Knuth
people.sub: Professor of Physics, University at Albany (SUNY); former NASA Ames research scientist; Editor-in-Chief, Entropy; Vice President, UAPx; research affiliate, The Galileo Project
people.narrative: Knuth wrote the paper that made the kinematics argument citable. A physicist with a PhD from Minnesota (1995) who spent 2001-2005 at NASA Ames designing AI algorithms for astrophysical data analysis before joining Albany in 2005, he is Editor-in-Chief of the MDPI journal Entropy and works in information physics and Bayesian inference. In September 2019 he published, with Robert Powell of the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies and Peter Reali, 'Estimating Flight Characteristics of Anomalous Unidentified Aerial Vehicles' in Entropy 21(10):939, deriving accelerations, speeds and required power from four documented cases including the 2004 Nimitz encounter. Whatever one thinks of the inputs, the paper did something no amount of testimony could: it put numbers with error bars into a peer-reviewed physics journal, and every subsequent argument about whether the observed performance is achievable with known propulsion has had to engage with it. He is Vice President of UAPx, a research affiliate of the Galileo Project, and co-author of the 2025 UAPx field-expedition paper. The editorship of Entropy is worth noting plainly: a journal editor publishing in his own journal invites the obvious criticism, and the paper's critics have made it.

people.label: Beatriz Villarroel
people.sub: Astronomer, Nordita / Stockholm University and Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias; principal investigator, VASCO (Vanishing and Appearing Sources during a Century of Observations)
people.narrative: Villarroel is running the one line of investigation that could produce hard evidence about the 1940s-1950s period without any cooperation from the US government at all, because her dataset predates the government's ability to classify it. VASCO compares the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey plates - exposed between 1949 and 1957, before any artificial satellite existed - against modern sky surveys, looking for point sources that appear in the old plates and are absent now. Anything genuinely transient and star-like on a pre-Sputnik plate cannot be a satellite glint, which makes the archive a clean natural experiment. Her group published the VASCO methodology in The Astronomical Journal in December 2019, then in June 2021 reported in Scientific Reports nine simultaneous transients on a single plate from 12 April 1950, and in 2022 published the 'glint in the eye' analysis in Acta Astronautica arguing photographic plate archives are a viable search space for non-terrestrial artefacts. Then, on 20 October 2025, she and Stephen Bruehl published in Scientific Reports the result that matters most for this board: transients in POSS-I 'may be associated with nuclear testing and reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena'. That is a peer-reviewed, Nature-portfolio paper drawing a statistical association between above-ground nuclear tests, contemporaneous UAP reports, and anomalous point sources on astronomical plates from the exact period this board treats as the programme's origin. The Sol Foundation made it the subject of its first policy briefing in January 2026.

people.label: Peter Skafish
people.sub: Sociocultural anthropologist and philosopher; co-founder and Executive Director, The Sol Foundation; member, UAP Science Advisory Council (2026)
people.narrative: Skafish is the institutional architect. An anthropologist and philosopher of science, he co-founded The Sol Foundation with Garry Nolan on 15 August 2023 and serves as its Executive Director, building the first organisation to treat UAP as simultaneously a materials-science problem, a governance problem and a public-understanding problem, and to publish on all three under one imprint. Sol's output is not advocacy ephemera: it is a numbered policy briefing series with named authors, including his own November 2024 paper 'The Prospect of Executive Branch Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Secrecy: The Harm to Congress and Potential Remedies', which argues the concealment case in institutional rather than sensational terms. He recruited into the foundation's orbit exactly the people whose signatures matter - Nolan on materials, Karl Nell on programme structure, Tim Gallaudet on the maritime domain, and Kirk McConnell, a thirty-seven-year Senate Armed Services and intelligence-committee staffer, as Senior Legislative Affairs Officer. That last hire is the tell: Sol went and got the staffer who had actually run the oversight paperwork. In June 2026 Skafish was named to the UAP Science Advisory Council as its cultural anthropologist, alongside Nolan and other Sol-affiliated figures.

people.label: Robert M. Powell

people.narrative: Powell is the person who made the radar-and-documents approach into a body of work. A chemist by training with a career in semiconductor engineering, he co-founded the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, a 501(c)(3) whose method is unglamorous and effective: obtain the primary sensor record through FOIA, reconstruct the event quantitatively, publish with the data attached. The 2010 Stephenville study with Glen Schulze reconstructed FAA radar returns around the January 2008 Texas sightings; the 2015 Aguadilla study with Morgan Beall, Larry Cates, Carl Paulson and Richard Hoffman analysed thermal imagery captured by a Department of Homeland Security Customs and Border Protection aircraft off Puerto Rico in April 2013 - a federal sensor record, obtained lawfully, analysed openly. He is second author of the Knuth-Powell-Reali Entropy paper of 2019, and lead author of the 2023 SCU study of reported shape, size, kinematics, electromagnetic effects and sound across a large report corpus. SCU also runs the Hancock-Porritt-Grosvenor series correlating 1945-1975 UAP activity with the United States atomic warfare complex, which is the documentary counterpart of Villarroel's plate work. SCU deposits its studies on Zenodo with DOIs, which means its output is citable and time-stamped rather than ephemeral.

people.label: Sarah Little
people.sub: Marine biochemist (PhD, MIT/WHOI); board member, Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies; co-author, Galileo Project geomagnetic variometer instrumentation paper
people.narrative: Little is one of the small number of people who work across both of the serious civil research programmes, which makes her a useful index of how thin the actual technical bench is. A marine biochemist trained through the MIT/Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution joint programme, she sits on the board of the Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies, where she co-authored the 2023 study of reported UAP shape, size, kinematics, electromagnetic effects and sound with Robert Powell and Larry Hancock, and she is a co-author on the Galileo Project's 2025 paper in Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems describing the deployment of a geomagnetic variometer station as auxiliary instrumentation for UAP study. entities.label: Galileo Project Pacific Ocean expedition to the CNEOS 2014-01-08 (IM1) site, June-July 2023
entities.sub: $1.6m magnetic-sled recovery of sub-millimetre spherules off Papua New Guinea
entities.desc: In June and July 2023 the Galileo Project conducted a fully funded expedition, budgeted at approximately $1.6 million, to the Pacific Ocean site of CNEOS 2014-01-08 - a 0.45-metre bolide that entered the atmosphere near the northeast coast of Papua New Guinea on 8 January 2014 and which Amir Siraj and Avi Loeb had argued, in The Astrophysical Journal in November 2022, had an apparently interstellar velocity. The team dragged a magnetic sled across the seabed at a location determined from seismometer data and recovered several hundred sub-millimetre spherules, which Loeb's group classified in Research Notes of the AAS (31 January 2024) and Chemical Geology (December 2024) as including a distinct composition they labelled 'BeLaU' - enriched in beryllium, lanthanum and uranium - which they argued was inconsistent with solar-system materials. The counter-argument arrived quickly and in the ordinary way. Patricio Gallardo argued in Research Notes of the AAS in October 2023 that anthropogenic coal ash could contaminate a micro-meteoritic underwater search. Steve Desch posted critiques in November 2023 and March 2024. Fernando et al. published in Geophysical Journal International in March 2024 showing that the seismic signal used to localise the search was more consistent with truck traffic than with an ocean impact - meaning the sled may have been dragged in the wrong place entirely. Rudraswami, Singh and Pandey published a re-evaluation of the spherules' proposed origin in Chemical Geology in March 2025. This expedition matters to the board as the control case: it is what a genuine, funded, public physical-recovery attempt looks like, including its failure modes, and every part of the argument - claim, rebuttal, re-analysis - happened in the peer-reviewed literature within eighteen months. That is the standard against which seventy years of unpublished government custody should be measured.

entities.desc: The custody domain tracks the documentary handoffs themselves rather than the objects. Its findings on this board are mostly negative and that is the point: To The Stars Academy's own chief operating officer, a former Lockheed Skunk Works advanced systems director, publicly conceded that the ADAM materials had been 'collected from sources with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation'. The DIA-funded AAWSAP DIRD series is exemplary at documenting the flow of paper - control numbers, fiscal years, named programme managers, contractor addresses - and silent on the flow of objects. No released document in the AAWSAP corpus records the receipt, transfer or storage of a physical sample. That asymmetry is the single most important structural observation in this domain: the government's own released record proves that it commissioned propulsion theory, materials science and injury pathology, and proves nothing about what it was holding while it did so.

entities.sub: Peer-reviewed journal of UAP studies, DOI prefix 10.59661
entities.desc: Limina is a peer-reviewed journal dedicated to UAP studies with its own DOI prefix, publishing since 2024. Its output includes methodological and governance work - Daniel Ammon on the development, dissemination and revision of good scientific practice for UAP research (January 2024) and on the demarcation problem (July 2026), Matthew Szydagis on disclosure timelines (March 2025), Karen Engels on phenomenology, James Houran on a procedural roadmap for scientific studies of government-sourced UAP data (July 2026), and the SCU Grosvenor-Hancock-Porritt analysis of the 1945-1975 United States atomic warfare complex (March 2025). Its existence matters institutionally rather than evidentially: a field cannot accumulate knowledge without a venue that will referee it, and until Limina and the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation special issue there was no such venue that a serious scientist could publish in without career cost. The journal is also where the argument about what would even count as government-sourced evidence is being conducted in print.

timeline.label: SRI psychoenergetics
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin the SRI International programme that becomes the government's Stargate effort - the template for outsourcing an unwanted phenomenon to a private laboratory.

timeline.label: Council Bluffs fall
timeline.text: Five independent witness groups see a luminous mass descend near Big Lake Park, Council Bluffs, Iowa; police photograph a four-by-six-foot molten metal mass. The sample survives into the modern literature.

timeline.label: First Council Bluffs analysis
timeline.text: The Des Moines Register reports the initial materials analyses identifying the metal as high-carbon steel and slag - the baseline the 2022 Stanford work would revisit.

timeline.label: IASA founded
timeline.text: Puthoff establishes the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, incorporated under EarthTech International in 1991.

timeline.label: Carnegie tests the Howe samples
timeline.text: Linda Moulton Howe says the bismuth/magnesium-zinc laminate was tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism, the first documented laboratory in that chain of custody.

timeline.label: Alleged Wilson meeting
timeline.text: The date attributed to Eric Davis's meeting with Vice Adm. Thomas R. Wilson recorded in the notes that surfaced in 2019 among Edgar Mitchell's papers, describing a special access programme that refused a former DIA director access.

timeline.label: 'Probable ET Generated' proposal to Puthoff
timeline.text: A proposal to analyse 'Probable ET Generated Specific Near-field Electromagnetic Emissions' is addressed to Puthoff and Hathaway - quoted verbatim in the preface of Kit Green's later DIRD, nine months before the AAWSAP contract.

timeline.label: AAWSAP awarded
timeline.text: The DIA awards the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications contract to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies; Colm Kelleher serves as deputy administrator.

timeline.label: DIRD series produced
timeline.text: The FY2009 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents are produced under the DIA Defense Warning Office with James T. Lacatski as programme manager - propulsion physics, exotic materials and human injury pathology commissioned as one set.

timeline.label: DIA-08-1004-004 issued
timeline.text: 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy' is issued with Eric W. Davis of EarthTech International, 11855 Research Blvd, Austin TX, named as author.

timeline.label: Puthoff's negative result
timeline.text: A letter from Puthoff reports that testing of the Howe samples produced no proof of alien origin and no 'interesting/anomalous outcome', with one test outstanding for want of equipment.

timeline.label: To The Stars Academy formed
timeline.text: Puthoff co-founds TTSA with Tom DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Steve Justice, creating a public-company vehicle for materials acquisition and analysis.

timeline.label: DIA releases the 38-title list
timeline.text: DIA responds to Steven Aftergood's FOIA request with the list of 38 AATIP research titles funded 2007-2012 at approximately $22 million, previously provided to Congress in January 2018.

timeline.label: ADAM Research Project announced
timeline.text: TTSA announces acquisition of 'potentially exotic materials'; COO Steve Justice concedes they came from sources 'with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation'.

timeline.label: Entropy kinematics paper

timeline.label: US Army CRADA signed
timeline.text: TTSA enters a five-year cooperative research and development agreement with the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command covering inertial mass reduction, metamaterials, quantum physics and beamed energy propulsion.

timeline.label: Kit Green DIRD released

timeline.label: Davis briefs a DoD agency
timeline.text: Davis gives a classified briefing to a Defense Department agency about retrievals from 'off-world vehicles not made on this earth'. The agency has never been identified.

timeline.label: 'We couldn't make it ourselves'
